what: Stretches the section to 600vh (three cards) and pins the stage to the screen. From a stack of overlapped photo cards, the top one is bound to scroll (scrub 1) and flies up — the first card to the upper left (−350, −350, −30°), the second to the upper right (+350, −350, +30°), tilting as it vanishes and revealing the card below. Every 150vh data-step changes to 1·2·3…, and the consumer css changes that section’s name, button, number dot and background color.

options.per: Scroll taken by one sheet (vh), default 150
options.span: Scroll while one sheet flies past (multiple of per), default 1.6
options.x: Distance (px) flown sideways, odd sections go left, default 350
options.y: Distance flown up and down (px), default −350
options.rotate: Tilt angle (deg, negative on odd sections), default 30
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Stage attached to the screen — holds cards and text
options.[data-fx-part=card]: Photo cards to stack — first card on top
options.height: Section height (vh), default card count × per — original 600
options.first: Scroll position where the first section starts to fly (vh after the section top reaches the top of the screen), default per
options.every: Gap between where each section starts to fly (vh), default per — unlike the original’s section-index gap (150), it is first cell height × 3 (about 233)

from.where: index.html three facilities (original .home-information — 600vh sticky, photo 01 starts at x −350 · y −350 · rotation −30 · autoAlpha 0, 02 at x 350, scrub 1, data-scroll = ceil(3 × progress/.75), per section background color #ebf0ef → #ece8e0 → #e8ebe2 .5s)

note: Text and dot lighting and background color changes inside the stage are done in css — a transition is applied when [data-step] changes. The original set the fly-through range as first cell height × 2 ~ ×3 + screen + 300px — here it is translated into per · span fitted to the screen height.
